title: MENA AI Observatory / Observatoire d'IA de la région MOAN
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to revolutionize various sectors critical to poverty reduction, inclusion and the public good, including agriculture, health care and education. Left unchecked, however, the benefits are not likely to be distributed equally. AI also has the potential to replicate and exacerbate societal biases and to be used irresponsibly or unethically. Given the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region's diverse cultural, social and political landscape, there is a need for a context-specific, multi-stakeholder and interdisciplinary approach to ensure that AI is governed, developed and deployed in a manner that is responsible, inclusive and for the benefit of society.  This project will facilitate knowledge and exchange on the responsible and inclusive governance, development and deployment of AI, strengthen the capacity of policymakers and decision-makers to respond to emerging challenges and opportunities, and create knowledge exchange and networking opportunities across the region and globally.  To achieve this, the MENA Observatory on Responsible AI will conduct in-depth studies on responsible AI for policy and practice, ensuring that AI technologies are aligned with ethical standards and societal needs. It will bridge the gap between research and practice by positioning findings and best practices or use by policymakers, practitioners, and the public. It will also foster a regional multi-stakeholder network and promote collaboration, enhancing the collective capacity to address AI-related challenges. By leveraging its extensive regional networks and partnerships, the MENA Observatory aims to become a leading force in responsible AI dialogues, contributing to the global discourse on responsible AI. / L'intelligence artificielle (IA) a le potentiel de révolutionner divers secteurs essentiels à la réduction de la pauvreté, à l'inclusion et au bien public, y compris l'agriculture, les soins de santé et l'éducation. Toutefois, si rien n'est fait, il est peu probable que les avantages soient répartis également. L'IA a également le potentiel de reproduire et d'exacerber les préjugés sociétaux et d'être utilisée de manière irresponsable ou contraire à l'éthique. Compte tenu du paysage culturel, social et politique diversifié de la région Moyen-Orient et Afrique du Nord (MOAN), il est nécessaire d'adopter une approche multipartite et interdisciplinaire propre au contexte pour garantir que l'IA est régie, développée et déployée d'une manière responsable, inclusive et au profit de la société. Ce projet facilitera les connaissances et l'échange sur la gouvernance, le développement et le déploiement responsables et inclusifs de l'IA, renforcera la capacité des décideurs et des décideuses à répondre aux nouveaux défis et aux nouvelles possibilités, et créera des possibilités d'échange de connaissances et de réseautage dans la région et à l'échelle mondiale. Pour ce faire, l'Observatoire du MOAN sur l'IA responsable mènera des études approfondies sur l'IA responsable pour les politiques et la pratique, en veillant à ce que les technologies d'IA soient alignées sur les normes éthiques et les besoins sociétaux. Il comblera l'écart entre la recherche et la pratique en positionnant les résultats et les pratiques exemplaires ou l'utilisation par les décideurs et décideuses, les praticiens et praticiennes et le public. Il favorisera également un réseau régional multipartite et favorisera les collaborations, renforçant ainsi la capacité collective de relever les défis liés à l'IA. En tirant parti de ses vastes réseaux et partenariats régionaux, l'Observatoire du MOAN vise à devenir une force de premier plan dans les dialogues responsables sur l'IA, contribuant au discours mondial sur l'IA responsable./Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to revolutionize various sectors critical to poverty reduction, inclusion and the public good, including agriculture, health care and education. title: Governing responsible artificial intelligence and data in the Middle East and North Africa / Gouvernance de l'intelligence artificielle et des données responsables au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique du Nord
description: The digital transformation of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, presents both opportunities and challenges. The rapid but uneven pace of the changes is exacerbating digital divides and entrenched inequalities and negatively impacting vulnerable population groups that do not have quality access or digital skills, such as women, migrants, and youth. These issues are aggravated by the difficult economic and social conditions in the region, new instabilities wrought by the pandemic, and complex regional politics. Neither the governments of the concerned countries nor their sizable young, educated populations are prepared for the impact of digital technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) on the future of work, education, or governance. IDRC-supported research indicates that data resources in the region are scarce and suggests that there is a need for better, more inclusive data governance and access. There is an absence of networking and connectedness and a lack of meaningful discussion about the challenges of AI and its governance. Processes for evidence and data to support policy formulation are also weak, while the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystems for data and AI are underdeveloped and lack support and incentives. Over the longer term, there is a need for broader, deeper data, and digital literacy and education. The aims of this project are to foster and build knowledge and discussions around responsible AI and data governance in the MENA region, develop networks of expertise, raise the profile of ongoing efforts, and influence the governance of these technologies in the region. The project will be grounded in a focus on well-being, protection of privacy and intimacy, equity, diversity, inclusion, and sustainability, and will facilitate public policies that promote the inclusive benefits of AI that will serve the population, while mitigating its potential costs and risks. / La transformation numérique de la région Moyen-Orient et Afrique du Nord (MENA), accélérée par la pandémie de COVID-19, présente à la fois des occasions et des défis. Le rythme rapide mais inégal de ces changements exacerbe les fossés numériques et les inégalités bien ancrées, et a une incidence négative sur les groupes de population vulnérables qui ne disposent pas d'un accès de qualité ou de compétences numériques, comme les femmes, les migrants et les jeunes. Ces problèmes sont aggravés par les conditions économiques et sociales difficiles dans la région, les nouvelles instabilités engendrées par la pandémie et la complexité de la politique régionale. Ni les gouvernements des pays concernés ni leurs importantes populations jeunes et éduquées ne sont préparés aux répercussions des technologies numériques comme l'intelligence artificielle (IA) sur l'avenir du travail, de l'éducation ou de la gouvernance. Les recherches soutenues par le CRDI indiquent que les ressources de données dans la région sont rares et suggèrent qu'il est nécessaire d'améliorer la gouvernance et l'accès aux données et de les rendre plus inclusifs. Il y a une absence de mise en réseau et de liens, et un manque de discussions significatives sur les défis de l'IA et de sa gouvernance. Les processus de preuves et de données pour soutenir la formulation des politiques sont également faibles, tandis que les écosystèmes d'innovation et d'entrepreneuriat pour les données et l'IA sont sous-développés et manquent de soutien et de mesures incitatives. À plus long terme, il est nécessaire de disposer de données plus vastes et plus approfondies, ainsi que d'une éducation et d'une culture numérique. Les objectifs de ce projet sont de favoriser et de développer les connaissances et les discussions autour de la gouvernance de l'IA et des données responsables dans la région MENA, de développer des réseaux d'expertise, de rehausser le profil des efforts en cours et d'influencer la gouvernance de ces technologies dans la région.

title: Governing responsible artificial intelligence and data in the Middle East and North Africa
description: The digital transformation of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, presents both opportunities and challenges. The rapid but uneven pace of the changes is exacerbating digital divides and entrenched inequalities and negatively impacting vulnerable population groups that do not have quality access or digital skills, such as women, migrants, and youth. These issues are aggravated by the difficult economic and social conditions in the region, new instabilities wrought by the pandemic, and complex regional politics. Neither the governments of the concerned countries nor their sizable young, educated populations are prepared for the impact of digital technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) on the future of work, education, or governance.   IDRC-supported research indicates that data resources in the region are scarce and suggests that there is a need for better, more inclusive data governance and access. There is an absence of networking and connectedness and a lack of meaningful discussion about the challenges of AI and its governance. Processes for evidence and data to support policy formulation are also weak, while the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystems for data and AI are underdeveloped and lack support and incentives. Over the longer term, there is a need for broader, deeper data, and digital literacy and education.   The aims of this project are to foster and build knowledge and discussions around responsible AI and data governance in the MENA region, develop networks of expertise, raise the profile of ongoing efforts, and influence the governance of these technologies in the region. The project will be grounded in a focus on well-being, protection of privacy and intimacy, equity, diversity, inclusion, and sustainability, and will facilitate public policies that promote the inclusive benefits of AI that will serve the population, while mitigating its potential costs and risks.

title: Strengthening the Open Data for Development Community in MENA
description: Data is an essential tool for achieving the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Data supports better monitoring and decision-making, improves public service delivery, and enables greater transparency and accountability in public spending. For data to be truly effective, a data eco-system must exist to improve data collection, management, and use for development.By joining the global Open Data for Development (OD4D) movement, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region continues to build a vibrant data community. Governments are increasingly interested in how open data can improve their services and they are looking for ways to build the capacity of their civil servants in this area. Almost every country in the region shows open government data activity, with Jordan and Tunisia leading the way as members of the Open Government Partnership (OGP), and Morocco exhibiting renewed interest in joining the partnership. Moreover, the potential of data-driven innovation to spur commercial activity is also garnering attention from governments in the region. The new data economy could potentially lead to billions in new economic activity. However, challenges remain in the areas of coordination, capacity building, data quality, privacy, and security. The creation of the MENA OD4D node is necessary to build a strategic network for the open data community in the region. Looking to mobilize the power of open data in various facets of development, the node will coordinate and participate in ongoing activities and research on open data in the region, bringing a focus to goals and aligning efforts to common challenges. It will identify gaps in the use of open data, support creation of standards, build capacity, support and assess policy, and streamline and harmonize efforts across the region. It is expected that this project, implemented with local partner the American University in Cairo, will result in strengthened research and advocacy capacity of the open data community in MENA. Its aim is to effectively address development challenges as well as build stronger connections with international open data initiatives and partners. It is also expected that the project's findings and recommendations will enhance commercial and civic innovation in different fields and inform policy debates around effective data collection and management and use of open data for development in the region, with a special focus on privacy, security, and quality issues.
